slides.title: ODD+LLM: Specifying LLM-Agent Behavior for Reproducible Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper introduces ODD+LLM, a protocol extension that standardizes the documentation of LLM-agent components like prompt assembly and memory serialization, addressing critical reproducibility gaps in social simulations relevant to MIMIC's hybrid human-AI modeling.

card.one_liner: ODD+LLM extends agent-based modeling standards to document LLM-specific behaviors for reproducible social simulations.
card.key_idea: Adds five documentation blocks covering prompt assembly, memory, parsing, and retry logic to the ODD protocol.
card.evaluation: Multiverse analysis of a naming-game simulation and a sufficiency review of 28 published papers showing 77% of details are undetermined.
card.limitation: Demonstration relies on a single case study with one model; protocol validity is not yet empirically proven.

slides.title: A Framework for Context Enrichment and Selective Robustness in LLM Social Agents
slides.highlight: This work addresses the brittleness of LLM agents in social simulations by proposing a framework for context enrichment and selective robustness, which is relevant to MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Framework for validating LLM social agents via controlled context enrichment and selective robustness testing.
card.key_idea: Decomposes context into five conditions and defines selective robustness as stability against surface variations plus responsiveness to meaningful social changes.
card.evaluation: Pilot study using Prisoner's Dilemma with GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra; measured surface sensitivity and world responsiveness across 40 prompt configurations.
card.limitation: Limited to one game setting and two models; grounded prompts may confound decision relevance with increased salience of world distinctions.

slides.title: Just Between Us? Exploring a Wearable-Mediated Channel for Discreet Human-Agent Interaction in a Shared Game Setting
slides.highlight: This study explores a wearable-mediated channel combining in-ear audio and head tilts to enable discreet human-agent interaction in shared settings, addressing the challenge of limiting co-present others' access to information.

card.one_liner: Wearable-mediated discreet interaction enables private human-agent communication in shared games without causing wearer stress.
card.key_idea: Combines in-ear audio messages with rightward head-tilt responses via eSense wearables to facilitate bidirectional, discreet human-agent interaction.
card.evaluation: 20 pairs played a card game; 39/40 turns succeeded. Wearers reported low tension and high usability, though non-wearer awareness varied.
card.limitation: Wizard-of-Oz setup limits autonomy; non-wearers sometimes noticed or inferred the channel, raising fairness and transparency concerns.

slides.title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation
slides.highlight: This work introduces selective departure forecasting with conformal risk guarantees for emotional dynamics in conversation, offering a method to detect changes in speaker state while controlling prediction errors. It is relevant to HyECHO as it provides a rigorous framework for modeling temporal engagement and emotional shifts in dyadic interactions without relying on massive data.

card.one_liner: Predicting emotional state changes outperforms value forecasting, enabling risk-controlled departure detection with conformal guarantees.
card.key_idea: Shifts target from emotional value to departure occurrence, using selective commitment policies and dialogue-level conformal risk control for guarantees.
card.evaluation: Tested on IEMOCAP, DailyDialog, MELD, EmoryNLP; metrics include CCC, LT-F1, AUROC; validated via leakage tests and conformal risk bounds.
card.limitation: Persistence barrier relies on oracle historical states; risk guarantees incur high abstention costs, reducing recall on some datasets.

slides.title: Same Method, Different Task: What the Bitter Lesson Does Not License in Social Simulation
slides.tldr: Bitter Lesson Limits in Social Simulation
slides.highlight: This paper argues that applying the 'bitter lesson' to social simulation by replacing hand-built agents with LLMs is flawed because prediction lacks the stakes inherent in cooperation and norm enforcement, a distinction critical for MIMIC's goal of modeling harmonious hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: LLMs fail social simulation because they lack stakes, not emergence, requiring mixed-motive training.
card.key_idea: Bitter lesson requires same-task scaling; LLMs predict text without stakes, missing cooperation's conflict-of-interest basis.
card.evaluation: 540-agent pilot in common-pool resource game; tested persistent consequences vs. stated payoffs across three model families.
card.limitation: Environment lacked genuine payoff externalities; results reflect responsiveness to state, not true interest or heterogeneity.

slides.title: Xinhua launches world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors demonstrates advanced human-robot interaction and embodied presence in public-facing roles, relevant to the development of socially engaging embodied AI.

slides.title: Xinhua Unveils Bionic Humanoid Robot News Anchors with UBTECH
slides.highlight: The deployment of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors demonstrates advanced human-robot interaction and embodied social presence in public-facing roles.

slides.title: Must AI Spell It Out? Pragmatic Comprehension of Alerts in a Time-Critical Task
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that users can effectively interpret underspecified alerts from AI systems that model listener knowledge, supporting more efficient human-AI communication in time-critical monitoring tasks.

card.one_liner: Pragmatic AI assistants that omit known information improve user detection speed and accuracy in time-critical monitoring tasks.
card.key_idea: An RSA-based planner adapts alert specificity to user prior knowledge, saving time by underspecifying known issues to alert on unknown ones.
card.evaluation: Preregistered study (N=114) in DroneWorld; pragmatic planner outperformed baseline in detection and speed, especially for low-awareness users.
card.limitation: Benefit was concentrated in low-awareness scenarios; high-awareness users showed no significant performance gain over the baseline.

slides.title: OpenZilo: An Open Smart-Ring Platform for Human-Centric Sensing and Interaction with Robots
slides.highlight: This paper introduces an open smart-ring platform for human-robot interaction, evaluating speech and gesture control alongside physiological-event triggers. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning by providing a wearable interface framework that connects user input to timely physical robot actions.

card.one_liner: OpenZilo is an open smart-ring platform linking multimodal sensing to robot execution for human-centric interaction.
card.key_idea: Integrates microphone, IMU, PPG, and temperature sensors with modular software separating acquisition, event interpretation, policy, and robot execution.
card.evaluation: Evaluated with 10 participants on speech/gesture commands and simulated physiological events; achieved ~90% task success rates.
card.limitation: Results rely on simulated physiological events and a small convenience sample, lacking real-world clinical validation or statistical significance.

slides.title: When Debate Amplifies Risk: Social-Bias Vulnerabilities in Multi-Agent Safety Deliberation
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates how social biases in multi-agent debate can amplify safety risks in retrieval-augmented systems, offering an inference-time auditing framework to mitigate these vulnerabilities.

card.one_liner: Multi-agent debate amplifies web safety risks via social bias; RiskTrace-Debias mitigates this using inference-time auditing.
card.key_idea: SafeConflict-Bias isolates social cues; RiskTrace-Debias enforces evidence-first precommitment, metadata masking, and consistency-gated arbitration.
card.evaluation: Tested on 700 instances across four models; reduces unsafe adoption from 100% to ≤2% without over-refusal, validated by ablations.
card.limitation: Relies on accurate evidence categorization in precommitment; masking may suppress valid contextual signals in complex debates.

slides.title: VIPBench: A Human-Aligned Benchmark for Voice Identity Perception in the Age of Voice Cloning
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR HUMAN PERCEPTION OF VOICE IDENTITY
slides.highlight: VIPBench evaluates how human listeners perceive voice identity across real, cloned, and morphed speech, revealing significant divergence between speaker-label accuracy and human judgment, which is critical for robust identity recognition in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: VIPBench evaluates speaker models against human voice identity perception, revealing significant divergence from metadata labels.
card.key_idea: 124k human judgments on real, cloned, and morphed voice pairs benchmark model alignment with perceived identity rather than ground-truth speaker labels.
card.evaluation: Tested 11 speech models on 4 tasks using Pearson correlation, AUC, and calibration metrics; best model explains 61% of explainable variance.
card.limitation: Models trained on metadata labels align poorly with human perception of clones, and no model reaches the human noise ceiling.

slides.title: Benchmarking Speaker Embedders in the Sub-Second Regime for Real-Time Voice AI Agents
slides.highlight: This study evaluates speaker embedders for separating active users from background speech in real-time voice agents, offering insights relevant to HyECHO's goal of robust identity recognition and diarization in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: Denoising harms sub-second speaker verification; TitaNet-Small on raw audio with truncated embeddings is optimal.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking speaker embedders under sub-second latency reveals denoising degrades EER, while TitaNet-Small on raw full-VAD chunks performs best.
card.evaluation: Tested on 400 real calls with injected interference and live production traffic, measuring EER and F1 across five architectures.
card.limitation: Findings are specific to a demographically homogeneous Hindi-speaking population; overlapping speech and diverse demographics remain unaddressed.

slides.title: Challenges, Opportunities, and Misconceptions in Neurosymbolic AI
slides.highlight: This paper addresses key challenges in neurosymbolic AI, such as semantic alignment and computational cost, which are critical for the neuro-symbolic agent models used in MIMIC's simulation of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Examines neurosymbolic AI challenges, opportunities, and misconceptions regarding efficiency, safety, and interpretability.
card.key_idea: Identifies semantic alignment and symbolic computational cost as major challenges, addressing misconceptions about differentiability and scalability.
card.evaluation: Qualitative synthesis from a 2026 CNRS workshop working group; no empirical benchmarks or quantitative results provided.
card.limitation: Not an exhaustive survey; lacks empirical validation or specific performance metrics for the discussed approaches.

slides.title: ReSUM: Reasoning-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Query-Focused Summarization
slides.highlight: This work addresses complex speaker dynamics and sparse key information in long meetings, which aligns with HyECHO's goal of robust multimodal social perception in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: ReSUM uses a multi-agent framework with reasoning distillation to improve query-focused meeting summarization.
card.key_idea: Decomposes tasks into planning, retrieval, summarization, and critique agents, using teacher-student CoT distillation for reasoning.
card.evaluation: Tested on QMSum and SQuALITY against zero-shot, RAG, and fine-tuned baselines using ROUGE, BERTScore, and human evaluation.
card.limitation: Relies on GPT-4-mini for planning/critique, potentially increasing cost and latency compared to single-model approaches.
